attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses the assessment in his own words.

semantics.note: In context, calling the one-year prospect 'bonkers' expresses a firm negative expectation. The normalization preserves the deadline and perfect-reliability threshold.

contract.note: The contract substitutes a selected summarization benchmark for the existence of any perfectly reliable chatbot. Nonzero scores establish failures among tested models; zero on one finite test would not establish perfect reliability. This substitution can determine the result.

evidence.note: The dated leaderboard fits the contract's near-deadline window and reports nonzero hallucination rates for all listed models. It supports the forecast for those tested models, but does not establish coverage of every available chatbot or the absence of other independent zero-result tests.

output.rationale: The deadline has passed. The leaderboard provides relevant evidence that tested models remained imperfect around February 2025. The packet does not settle whether any qualifying chatbot existed by the deadline, and its single-source search does not establish the contract's broader absence condition. Treating this benchmark as decisive requires an interpretation Marcus did not supply.
